frame.system_boundary: Municipal heat-response services, participating buildings, mobility, and affected residents

stakeholders.name: Residents at elevated heat risk
stakeholders.vulnerability: Age, health, housing, mobility, or outdoor exposure

invariants.name: Maximum modeled heat-health burden
invariants.rationale: Severe health burden cannot be compensated by cost or convenience

invariants.name: Minimum safe-cooling access
invariants.measure: Fraction of residents able to reach or retain safe cooling
invariants.rationale: A strategy is not viable if a material share of residents cannot use it

candidates.name: Central cooling centers with shuttle backup
candidates.initial_action: Expand large municipal cooling centers and provide event-triggered shuttle service
triggers: Open centers when heat alert is issued
irreversible_commitments: Long-term leases for three central facilities

candidates.name: Distributed passive protection and neighborhood hubs
candidates.initial_action: Combine home retrofits, shaded neighborhood hubs, microgrids, and mobile outreach
triggers: Island hub microgrids on grid instability

candidates.name: Public alerts with existing services
candidates.initial_action: Rely on heat alerts and existing emergency facilities

scenarios.name: Ordinary severe heatwave
scenarios.description: Seven days above the local severe-heat threshold

scenarios.name: Heatwave with multi-day grid outage
scenarios.description: Extreme heat raises load and coincides with a 72-hour outage

scenarios.name: Wildfire smoke and extreme heat
scenarios.description: Outdoor air is unsafe while cooling demand is elevated

scenarios.name: Transit disruption during heat emergency
scenarios.description: Road and public-transit capacity fall below half of normal

governance.decision_rule: Reject non-compensable failures and prohibited burden transfers, then present the Pareto frontier for accountable municipal selection

comparison_dimensions.name: worst_viability_margin
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Protect the thinnest remaining safety margin

comparison_dimensions.name: common_mode_exposure
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Avoid one dependency disabling all response paths

comparison_dimensions.name: maximum_externality_magnitude
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Minimize the largest normalized shifted harm without summing unlike harms

comparison_dimensions.name: annual_cost_musd
comparison_dimensions.rationale: Preserve public resources after viability is secured

veto_rules: Public health officer may veto a candidate that violates the health invariant
governance.appeal_process: Publish assumptions and accept a documented council reconsideration request
governance.dissent_process: Attach minority council and affected-community statements to the decision record
governance.review_schedule: Before each heat season and after every activation

evidence.source: Synthetic fixture based on a municipal heat-health model
evidence.limitations: Illustrative values; not a real municipal forecast

evidence.claim: Scenario-specific service access and recovery estimates
Central access controls may exclude high-risk residents

claims.statement: The supplied fixture calculates candidate-specific heat-health, access, recovery, and cost outcomes for the declared scenarios.

assertions.basis: The fixture contains explicit scenario outputs from the two declared synthetic models.

claims.limitations: This does not establish empirical accuracy, policy authorization, adoption, deployment, or observed public-health benefit.

claims.statement: Central access controls may exclude some high-risk residents during an extreme-heat response.
claims.scope: Risk hypothesis raised by the affected-community review

assertions.basis: The synthetic community review identifies a plausible exclusion pathway.

claims.limitations: The fixture does not provide an empirical observation or measured exclusion rate.

dissent.author: Budget office
dissent.position: The distributed strategy has a higher first-year budget requirement
